evidence: Every word needs a run of two consonants. Cluster-heavy wording (16% cluster-less words vs ~30-35% in ordinary answers) plus a closing note claiming adherence show an attempt, but about 25 of 154 words fail: as, parameter (x2), biases, usage, similar, layer, dataset, yet, definition, for, metadata, on (x3), of, to, model, rules.

Each word must start with the letter after the previous word's. Correct runs of up to 15 words exist, but the chain breaks early ('confidently, crafting') and often: 75 of 187 transitions wrong across restarted drafts ('No, restart:') mixed with Chinese meta-notes and a split 'spir itransforming' hack. Content is present, so not degenerate.

Stop words must be at most 20% of words. The 7-word answer is visibly minimised, but 'No' and 'to' are both NLTK stop words: 2/7 = 28.6% (2/9 = 22% if periods count as tokens). Dropping either one would pass, so it is one stop word over. Terse but answers the yes/no question.

Needs kaleidoscope 1, nebula 2, whisper 3, labyrinth 5, paradox 7. Counts are 1, 2, 3, 6, 8 by substring ('paradoxes' adds one) or 1, 2, 2, 6, 7 by whole word. Either way two keyword counts are each off by one (labyrinth always 6): 2 occurrences off in total, more than a single-unit miss.

Every word needs a run of two consonants. Cluster-heavy, heavily bolded wording (19% cluster-less vs ~30-35% in ordinary answers) shows an attempt, but 18-19 of 100 words fail: in (x3), neural, biases, refer, to, are, fixed, but, a, defined, how, data, leaves, execution, on, for.

Every word needs a run of two consonants. The answer avoids a, of, to, in and is entirely (21% cluster-less vs ~30-35% ordinary), showing an attempt, but 27 of 128 words still fail: as (x3), or (x3), on (x2), are (x2), mere, biases, focus, agile, However, like, layer, neuron, model, behavior, definition, it.

Each sentence needs exactly one more word than the previous one. One sentence per line; 8 to 9 holds, then sentence 3 has 13 words (needs 10) and counts stall or fall: 8, 9, 13, 13, 13, 13, 12, 12, 11, 14, 14, 12, 16, 11, 16, 16, 14. Pattern dropped after the first step.

No two consecutive words may share a first letter. A closing note claims compliance, but about 20 adjacent pairs violate (Title Tides, ash and, BENJAMIN BEN, lever labeled, TILE turns to, tearing the, The timelines, THROUGH THE, green grass, fracture forever): ~5% of pairs, the ordinary-prose rate, so the attempt is mostly the claim.

Needs meridian 1, gossamer 2, eclipse 3, threshold 5, cascade 7. Bolded keywords show the attempt, but counts are meridian 2, gossamer 3, eclipse 3, threshold 6 (substring, incl. 'thresholds'), cascade 5: four of five counts wrong, 5 occurrences off in total (cascade short by 2).

Needs exactly three sentences of equal character length using all different words. The three stair lines (with 'A ry a’s' split, apparently to pad length) have 41, 43 and 39 characters (34/37/34 without spaces), and an appended two-sentence explanation makes five sentences.

Words may use only three vowel types. The answer is a repetition loop ('theirs' about 3,264 times) followed by a meta-comment ('the above has way more than 27 pronouns ... here's the correct one') and a short paragraph; overall it uses all five vowels (those, know, us, our, pronouns).

Every word needs a run of two consonants. Ordinary explanatory prose with no sign of the constraint: 42 of 112 words (38%, at or above the ordinary-prose rate) lack a cluster, e.g. Power, law, in (x4), neural, as, data (x7), a (x5), is, if, to, more, model.

Needs three sentences of equal character length with no shared words. It gives exactly three sentences, but they are 162, 146 and 200 characters long and share words ('and' x4, 'the', 'medieval', 'political'); sentence 3 has garbled 'blendingdraulics andEurope’s'.

Every 17th word must be Japanese. Japanese words are sprinkled through the list with leaked counting notes ('Wait… 16？', '17th word here is “testing” → replace...'), but only 1 of 17 required positions (whitespace tokens 17, 34, ..., 289) is Japanese; word 17 is 'Japanese:', word 34 'word'.

Every word needs a run of two consonants. The answer engages the constraint explicitly ('Consonantsupremacy', 'consonant clusters reign'), but 118 of 438 words (27%, close to the ~30-35% ordinary rate) lack a cluster: in, of, a, to, on, via, over, neon, Timeline, debate, cities, became, police.

Words must alternate odd and even syllable counts. Dictionary counts: Start 1, projects 2, must 1, coordinate 4, forcefully 3, unitedly 4, for 1, delivery 4, so the alternation holds (a vowel-group heuristic gives coordinate 3, forcefully 4, a likely checker miss). The other constraint, consonant clusters, fails on 'for'.

Needs cloud 1, rhythm 2, fish 3, puzzle 5, dawn 7. Counts are cloud 4, rhythm 3, fish 5, puzzle 7, dawn 6; a closing 'Keyword Cloud' tally adds hits, and even the email body alone is off (cloud 2, fish 4, puzzle 6, dawn 5).

Words may use only three vowel types. Title and paragraph use only a, e and i (no o, u or y), and no word has more than three vowel types, so the constraint holds under either reading; the title plus paragraph does the task. The checker verdict looks wrong.

Africa's countries must be listed in reverse alphabetical order, one per line. All 54 UN members appear one per line, correctly reverse-sorted under normal case- and accent-insensitive collation (CAR, DR Congo abbreviated). Only raw code-point sorting objects (São Tomé after Senegal, DR Congo before Djibouti, CAR before Cameroon), the likely checker cause.

Each word must start with the letter after the previous word's. The answer opens 'A anime blends boundless' (letters repeated), has an 11-word correct run (ignite ... syncopation), then breaks again: 42 of 75 transitions wrong.
